transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you in today?

I guess I’m here because the clinic’s been on me about how little I’ve been eating. Most days I just have coffee before I go to the warehouse, and maybe later I’ll have a yogurt or a few bites of something after GED class. Sitting down for a real meal just feels like it messes up everything I’m trying to keep in line.
Do you avoid eating certain foods or restrict your eating because you’re afraid of gaining weight?

Yeah. I try to stay away from stuff like fried food in the break room, or if there’s a big plate at church. If I eat it, I start worrying it’s going to show on me right away, and then I can’t stop thinking about it. I just want to check the scale after.
After you eat, do you ever make yourself vomit, take laxatives, or exercise a lot more than usual to try to keep from gaining weight?
I don’t really know. I mean, I worry after I eat, but… I don’t think I have anything specific like that to tell you.
Do you ever push yourself to exercise a lot more than usual after eating to keep from gaining weight?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’m on my feet a lot at work, but I don’t really go out and exercise extra after eating or anything like that.
Have you ever made yourself throw up or done anything else right after eating to try to control your weight or keep from gaining weight?
No, I don’t make myself throw up. I don’t really do anything right after eating like that. I mostly just get worried in my head.
Do you ever feel like you’ve eaten a very large amount of food in a short period, more than most people would eat in similar circumstances?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve had times where it was, like, a huge amount in a short time. I mostly just feel worried about what I ate, even if it wasn’t that much.
Does worrying about food or your weight cause you a lot of distress or make it hard for you to do things you need to do in your daily life, like work or spend time with family?

Yeah… it does. I still go to work and I’m still going to class, but it gets in the way. I’ve been saying no to meals after church, and sometimes I leave my GED homework unfinished because I’m so stuck on keeping my eating and my schedule controlled. It’s hard to focus on anything else.
Have you ever felt like you couldn’t stop yourself from eating even when you weren’t hungry, or eaten a lot more than you meant to in a short amount of time?
No, I don’t think so. I can’t really remember feeling out of control like that. Sometimes I feel bad after eating, but it’s not like I couldn’t stop myself or ate a huge amount all at once.
Have you ever used any methods like self-induced vomiting, laxatives, diuretics, or excessive exercise specifically to prevent weight gain?
I’m not sure… I don’t think I’ve done those things, like making myself throw up or taking pills for it. I do try to control what I eat, but I don’t really have anything like that to tell you.
Even if you were underweight, would the idea of gaining any weight feel completely unacceptable to you, or do you feel like being thin is extremely important to your self-worth?

Yeah… I think it would feel really hard to accept gaining weight. Like, when I look in the mirror before class or before softball, my stomach and thighs still look bigger than they should to me. And it kind of decides how I feel about myself that day—like I’m doing good or I’m failing.
Would you say that your weight or body shape has a very strong influence on how you feel about yourself overall?

Yes. I mean, it really does. If I look in the mirror before class or softball and my stomach or thighs look too big to me, it can kind of ruin the whole day. I feel like I’m either doing okay or I’m failing, just based on that.
Do you restrict your eating because you genuinely aren't interested in food, or is it more because you're concerned about your body shape or weight?

It’s more because I’m worried about my weight and how I look. Like if I eat something fried from the break room, or a big plate at church, I start thinking it’s going to show on me right away. Then I keep thinking about it and want to check the scale.
Do you judge yourself mainly based on your body weight or shape, feeling that they are the most important things about you?

Yeah, I think I do. Like, if I look in the mirror and my stomach or thighs seem too big, it makes me feel like I’m failing for the day. If I think I look okay, then I feel better about myself. It matters more than I wish it did.
